prompt_text: Who is the best roofer in Denver for hail damage repair?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single definitive “best” roofer for hail damage in Denver — the right contractor depends on your exact location, the size of the job, your insurance situation, and the contractor’s experience with hail claims. I can, however, tell you how to find a high-quality roofer and what to watch for, and I can pull a short list of well-rated local companies if you give me your ZIP code.

How to pick a roofer for hail damage
- Verify experience with hail/insurance claims: ask how many hail jobs they do per year and whether they work directly with insurance adjusters.  
- Certifications: look for manufacturer certifications (GAF Master Elite, CertainTeed SELECT ShingleMaster, Owens Corning Preferred Contractor). These matter for material warranties.  
- Licensing and insurance: confirm the company carries general liability and workers’ compensation, and check for any required local business or contractor registration. Denver requires permits for roof replacements — ask who pulls permits.  
- References & reviews: check Google, Yelp, BBB, and local Facebook groups. Ask for recent references from hail jobs in the Denver area.  
- Written estimate and scope: get at least 3 written estimates that list materials, ventilation, flashing, underlayment, decking replacement policy, and timelines. Make sure estimates match the scope in your insurer’s estimate (or explain differences).  
- Warranty: ask about workmanship and manufacturer warranties and get them in writing.  
- Local presence: prefer contractors with a permanent Denver-area office and local crews (less chance of “storm-chaser” behavior).

Red flags to avoid
- High-pressure sales (insisting you must sign immediately).  
- Demands for large upfront payments (more than a reasonable deposit).  
- No written contract or unwillingness to provide references.  
- Claims they can “guarantee” an insurance payout or instruct you to misrepresent damage.  
- No permits pulled or refusal to pull permits.

Immediate steps if you have hail damage
- Document damage with photos (shingles, siding, vehicles).  
- Contact your insurer to report the claim.  
- Get 3 estimates from reputable roofers.  
- If leaks are present, ask for temporary tarping to prevent further interior damage.

If you want, I can:
- Find and compare 3–5 top-rated hail specialists near you (give me your ZIP code).  
- Provide a short checklist you can give contractors during walkthroughs.  

Which would you prefer?
